newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelans snap up CANTV, orders top $195.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelans snap up CANTV, orders top $195.5 mln.

text.p: Venezuelan investors have so far placed orders for some 91.88 billion bolivars ($195.5 million) worth of shares in national telephone company CANTV, official sources told Reuters, only a hair below the government's $200 million target.
"By Monday, some 4.9 billion bolivars ($10.43 million) of that came from local institutional investors, the rest from small investors," said the source, who asked to remain anonymous.
"It's clear that the government's $200 million target for the local market will be surpassed," he added.
Bidding for the local portion of the issue close this afternoon at 1630 local time/1530 EST. International bidding on the issue closes Thursday afternoon.

Fifty million shares are being offered on the local market in the 289 million global share offering, although the Venezuelan National Investment Fund (FIV) is holding back a further 75 million in case of excess demand.
Final pricing of the issue is due to take place Thursday. The early reference range put the issue at between $3.07 and $3.50, although the final price may be higher.
Last week, the FIV said it expected total buy orders reach around $900 million.
